newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stock market ends lower ahead of weekend.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stock market ends lower ahead of weekend.

text.p: Singapore shares ended the week lower as retail investors took profits ahead of the weekend and the corporate results reporting season in March, dealers said.
"It's just punters taking profit ahead of the weekend," said one dealer who added that investors' mood generally turned cautious as the results reporting season approached.
The Straits Times Industrials Index ended down 10.70 points at 2,241.28. Turnover was a healthy 447 million shares with losers outpacing gainers by 214 to 181.
Small-capitalised local shares like Nobel Design, Wee Poh and Pacific Andes were active.
Malaysia's paper and property investment company Insas Bhd led the actives with over 24 million shares. The stock hit a new high at Singapore $1.27 before ending at S$1.26, up S$0.07.

News that U.S. Cyrix Corp would supply Compaq Computer with a new low-cost microprocessor failed to dampen electronic shares and those linked to rival Intel. "There is no impact because the low-end chip market actually accounts for a small portion of the semi-conductor market," said one dealer.
Malaysia's Samanda Holdings led gainers while selected blue including property stocks fell on fears of weaker full year results. -- Angela Tan (65 8703083)
